capex.heading: Capital Expenditures
capex.text:
Included in cash flows from investing activities are capital maintenance expenditures and capital project expenditures. Capital maintenance expenditures relate to the replacement of existing fixed assets with a useful life greater than one year that are obsolete, exhausted, or no longer cost effective to repair. Capital project expenditures represent fixed asset additions related to land or building improvements to new or existing assets or purchases of new (non-replacement) equipment or software related to specific projects deemed necessary expenditures.

We spent $204.7 million in 2025 on project capital investments including: Churchill Downs Racetrack, Roseshire, Owensboro, Marshall Yards, and Rosie's Richmond. We currently expect our project capital to be approximately $180.0 to $220.0 million in 2026, although this amount may vary significantly based on the timing of work completed, unanticipated delays, and timing of payments to third parties.

intro.text: Churchill Downs Incorporated ("CDI" or the "Company") has been creating extraordinary entertainment experiences for over 150 years, beginning with the Company’s most iconic and enduring asset, the Kentucky Derby. Headquartered in Louisville, Kentucky, CDI has expanded through the acquisition, development, and operation of live and historical racing entertainment venues, the growth of the online wagering businesses, and the acquisition, development, and operation of regional casino gaming properties. The Company manages its business through three reportable segments: Live and Historical Racing, Wagering Services and Solutions, and Gaming. We aggregate our other businesses as well as certain corporate operations in All Other. We report net revenue and operating expense associated with these reportable segments and other information about these segments in Part II, Item 8.

capex.heading: Capital Expenditures
capex.text:
Included in cash flows from investing activities are capital maintenance expenditures and capital project expenditures. Capital maintenance expenditures relate to the replacement of existing fixed assets with a useful life greater than one year that are obsolete, exhausted, or no longer cost effective to repair. Capital project expenditures represent fixed asset additions related to land or building improvements to new or existing assets or purchases of new (non-replacement) equipment or software related to specific projects deemed necessary expenditures.

We have spent $463.4 million in 2024 on project capital investments including: Churchill Downs Racetrack Paddock Project, the Terre Haute Casino Resort in Vigo County, Indiana, The Rose Gaming Resort in Northern Virginia, and Owensboro Racing & Gaming in Western Kentucky. We currently expect our project capital to be approximately $350 to $400 million in 2025, although this amount may vary significantly based on the timing of work completed, unanticipated delays, and timing of payments to third parties.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Horse racing, pari-mutuel wagering, and casino gaming businesses depend on the public perception of integrity and fairness in their operations.
Our success depends upon new product development and technological advancements, including the development of new wagering platforms and features.
A substantial majority of the slot and HRM machines sold in the U.S. are manufactured by a few select companies.
We rely on a limited number of vendors to provide video poker, slot and HRM machines and any loss of equipment suppliers could impact our operations.
We rely on a variety of hardware and software products to maximize revenue and efficiency in our operations.
We rely on vendors that may use components produced in foreign countries.

Our operations in certain jurisdictions depend on agreements with industry constituents including horsemen and other racetracks, and the failure to enter into or maintain these agreements on terms acceptable to us could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, and financial condition
Our operations in certain jurisdictions depend on agreements with third parties.
We rely on information technology and other systems to manage our business and our operations rely heavily on technology services.
Our online wagering, HRM and brick-and-mortar casino businesses depend upon our communications hardware and our computer hardware.
We rely on third parties to provide payment-processing services, and it could disrupt our business if these companies become unwilling or unable to provide these services to us.
Our Live and Historical Racing segment is subject to extensive state and local regulation, and we depend on continued state approval of legalized pari-mutuel wagering in states where we operate.

Our primary sources of liquidity and capital resources have been and will continue to be cash flow from operations, borrowings under our credit facility, and proceeds from the issuance of debt securities.

x.name: Rivers Des Plaines
f: Equity method investment, difference between carrying amount and underlying equity

s.t: As of September 30, 2026 , the net aggregate basis difference between the Company’s investment in Rivers Des Plaines and the amounts of the underlying equity in net assets was $ 833 million.
Our investment in Rivers Des Plaines was $ 583 million and $ 573 million as of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, respectively.
Both the Company and High Plaines have participating rights over Rivers Des Plaines, and both must consent to certain operating, investing and financing decisions.

Investments in and advances to unconsolidated affiliates as of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, primarily consisted of interests in Rivers Casino Des Plaines ("Rivers Des Plaines") and Miami Valley Gaming and Racing ("MVG").
As a result, we account for Rivers Des Plaines using the equity method.
• Rivers Des Plaines' impact on our investments in unconsolidated affiliates from legal reserves and transaction costs;
Our equity investments increased $3 million from strong performance at Rivers Des Plaines in Illinois and Miami Valley Gaming in Ohio.

x.name: Midwest Gaming Holdings, LLC
f: Carrying value of equity method investment
Carrying value of equity method investment

s.t: Following the point at which the Company gained 61.3 % interest in Midwest Gaming, the carrying value of the Company's investment was $ 835.0 million higher than the Company’s underlying equity in the net assets of Midwest Gaming.
Our equity investments decreased $8.4 million due to a $7.8 million decrease from Rivers Des Plaines due to increased competition and a $0.6 million decrease from Miami Valley Gaming.
As of December 31, 2025 , the net aggregate basis difference between the Company’s investment in Midwest Gaming and the amounts of the underlying equity in net assets was $ 833.2 million.
Both the Company and High Plaines have participating rights over Rivers Des Plaines, and both must consent to certain operating, investing, and financing decisions.

We also recognized a $ 103.2 million deferred tax liability and a corresponding increase in our investment in unconsolidated affiliates related to an entity we acquired in conjunction with our acquisition of the Clairvest ownership stake in Midwest Gaming.

The Company’s investment in Midwest Gaming is presented at our initial cost of investment plus the Company's accumulated proportional share of income or loss, including depreciation/accretion of the difference in the historical basis of the Company’s contribution, less any distributions it has received.
The Company has a 50% equity investment in Miami Valley Gaming and Racing ("MVG").
• Rivers Des Plaines' impact on our investments in unconsolidated affiliates from legal reserves and transaction costs;

Investments in and advances to unconsolidated affiliates as of December 31, 2025 and 2024 primarily consisted of interests in Rivers Casino Des Plaines ("Rivers Des Plaines") and Miami Valley Gaming and Racing ("MVG").
As a result, we account for Rivers Des Plaines using the equity method.

The summarized income statement information for 2025 and 2024 and summarized balance sheet information as of December 31, 2025 and 2024 includes the following equity investments: MVG and Rivers Des Plaines.
